scenario.name: Jeffrey Appel & Microsoft Threat Intel — ARTEX Multi-Agent LLM Framework: Machine-Speed Kill-Chain Compression, Storm-0940 Spray & Defender XDR Disruption
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security · T1595.002
scenario.overview: Imagine a lively downtown city street intersection with painted zebra crosswalks, glowing red-yellow-green traffic lights, corner shop awnings, and passing yellow taxis. At the busy downtown street corner, an impostor wearing a reflective utility vest kneels beside the metal traffic-signal control cabinet while pedestrians cross the street. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the marked pedestrian crosswalk disguised as a regular visitor, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station. The city intersection camera and municipal traffic control board detect the impossible all-green light timing and dispatch a traffic officer immediately. In this scenario (T1595.002, Jeffrey Appel & Microsoft Threat Intel, ARTEX Multi-Agent LLM Framework: Machine-Speed Kill-Chain Compression, Storm-0940 Spray & Defender XDR Disruption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: aRTEX Planner-Worker LLM Initialization, then machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence, then 5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ARTEX Planner-Worker LLM Initialization, then Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence, then 5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 50126 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.subtitle: Reconnaissance & Initial Access (T1595.002 - Vulnerability Scanning / T1110.003 - Password Spraying)
stages.description: At the busy downtown street corner, an impostor wearing a reflective utility vest kneels beside the metal traffic-signal control cabinet while pedestrians cross the street. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder approaches the marked pedestrian crosswalk disguised as a regular visitor while everyday visitors and the traffic officer go about their routine. The attacker launches the ARTEX Go server (artex-server --model deepseek-chat) and Next.js operator console, where a central LLM Planner decomposes the objective into autonomous Worker tasks (executing parallel nmap -sV -T4, curl endpoint fingerprinting, and Storm-0940 distributed password spraying against Entra ID and perimeter VPN endpoints to compromise an initial identity in minutes) (logged in SIEM Event 50126 with AgentArchitecture=ARTEX Go Planner-Worker Multi-Agent LLM Framework, InitialAccessVector=Storm-0940 Password Spraying + Automated Surface Recon , T1110.003 / T1595.002, ReferenceUrl=https://jeffreyappel.nl/artex-old-attacks-at-machine-speed-and-how-microsoft-defender-keeps-up/ so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes artex-server --planner-model deepseek-reasoner --worker-concurrency 8 --target corp.local (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , artex-server --planner-model deepseek-reasoner --worker-concurrency 8 --target corp.local vi so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1595.002 during "ARTEX Planner-Worker LLM Initialization, Autonomous nmap/curl Recon & Storm-0940 Password Spray" , The attacker launches the ARTEX Go server , artex-server --model deepseek-chat and Next while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence (`T1505.003`), Automated Kerberoasting (`0x17`) & Lateral Pivot
stages.subtitle: Persistence, Credential Access & Lateral Movement (T1505.003 - Web Shell / T1558.003 - Kerberoasting)
stages.description: Opening the unlocked cabinet panel, the impostor rewires the corner traffic light timer so every lane turns green at once and steers a yellow taxi down a side alley. Here in Step 2 inside the city street, the intruder moves quietly past the marked pedestrian crosswalk into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the neighboring sidewalk cafe. Without waiting for human operator review, the ARTEX Planner parses the valid credential output and immediately dispatches a Lateral Movement Worker agent that drops an obfuscated web shell for persistence, enumerates Active Directory SPNs (servicePrincipalName=*), requests RC4-downgraded Kerberos TGS tickets (EventID 4769, EncryptionType = 0x17), and pivots across hybrid servers in under 15 minutes (logged in Windows Security Event 4769 with KillChainCompression=Initial Spray to Web Shell + Kerberoast in 8 minutes 32 seconds, TicketEncryptionType=0x17 , RC4-HMAC Downgrade, MITRE T1558.003, WebShellParent=w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe / powershell.exe , T1505.003 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Worker-Persist: curl -X PUT https://10.10.20.14/owa/auth/healthcheck.aspx (Web shell drop via compromised admin session) (which executes the HTTP/HTTPS transfer client , Worker-Persist: curl -X PUT https://10.10.20.14/owa/auth/healthcheck.aspx , Web shell drop via compromise so that delivers the network exploit payload or retrieves the next-stage execution script , T1505.003 during "Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence , T1505.003, Automated Kerberoasting , 0x17 & Lateral Pivot" over HTTP/HTTPS). Next, the follow-up artifact Worker-AD: Invoke-Kerberoast / Rubeus.exe kerberoast /rc4opsec (Requests EventID 4769 TGS with TicketEncryptionType = 0x17) runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1505.003 during "Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence , T1505.003, Automated Kerberoasting , 0x17 & Lateral Pivot" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ c:\windows\system32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe -ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool" / ⇠#2 ACK 4769) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Perimeter VPN / Entra ID Identity Edge (Storm-0940 Password Spray)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Entra ID OAuth Apps & Azure Key Vault (5-Minute Secret Exfil)).

stages.title: Stage 3: 5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration (`Azure Key Vault`) & Defender XDR Automatic Attack Disruption
stages.subtitle: Credential Access, Exfiltration & Defensive Disruption (T1552.004 - Cloud Secrets / T1098.003 - Additional Cloud Roles)
stages.description: Traffic signals flip out of rhythm across the city intersection, creating instant confusion that lets an unmarked courier slip past the corner storefront unseen. In this final step inside the city street, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station until the intersection traffic camera catches the mismatch. Pivoting from hybrid credentials or leaked GitHub/CI secrets into Azure within 5 minutes, the ARTEX Cloud Worker enumerates Entra ID OAuth app permissions and issues rapid KeyVaultGetSecret calls across production vaults. Microsoft Defender XDR correlates the multi-domain alert burst (AlertInfo + AlertEvidence across Endpoint, Identity, and Cloud Apps within a 10-minute window) and triggers Automatic Attack Disruption, isolating the host via sense.exe and revoking all Entra refresh tokens (Revoke-MgUserSignInSession) (logged in SIEM Event 200 with CloudTarget=Azure Key Vault , Bulk SecretGet Enumeration, T1552.004, DetectionMechanism=KQL Multi-Alert Burst Correlation , Endpoint + Identity + Cloud Apps in < 15m, AutomatedDefense=Microsoft Defender XDR Automatic Attack Disruption , Host Isolation + Token Revocation so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Worker-Cloud: az keyvault secret list --vault-name corp-prod-kv && az keyvault secret show --name prod-db-conn-string (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , Worker-Cloud: az keyvault secret list --vault-name corp-prod-kv && az keyvault secret show so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.004 during "5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration , Azure Key Vault & Defender XDR Automatic Attack Disruption" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact KQL Burst Hunt: AlertInfo | join AlertEvidence on AlertId | summarize AlertCount=dcount(AlertId), Categories=make_set(Category) by DeviceId, AccountUpn, bin(Timestamp, 15m) | where AlertCount >= 3 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , KQL Burst Hunt: AlertInfo | join AlertEvidence on AlertId | summarize AlertCount=dcount, Ale so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.004 during "5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration , Azure Key Vault & Defender XDR Automatic Attack Disruption" , Pivoting from hybrid credentials or leaked GitHub/CI secrets into Azure within 5 minutes, the ARTEX Cloud Worker enumerates Entra ID OAuth app permissions and issues rapid KeyVaultGetSecret calls across production vaults while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GET https://corp-prod-kv.vault.azure.net/secrets/prod-sql-master-key?api-version=7.4 / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Perimeter VPN / Entra ID Identity Edge (Storm-0940 Password Spray)) to Node ④ (#4 Hybrid Windows Server (Web Shell Staging & RC4 Kerberoasting)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Entra ID OAuth Apps & Azure Key Vault (5-Minute Secret Exfil)).

briefing.headline: Scenario Briefing: Official DFIR & Log Forensics Guide for Jeffrey Appel & Microsoft Threat Intel, ARTEX Multi-Agent LLM Framework: Machine-Speed Kill-Chain Compression, Storm-0940 Spray & Defender XDR Disruption
briefing.storyAnalogy: Imagine a lively downtown city street intersection with painted zebra crosswalks, glowing red-yellow-green traffic lights, corner shop awnings, and passing yellow taxis. At the busy downtown street corner, an impostor wearing a reflective utility vest kneels beside the metal traffic-signal control cabinet while pedestrians cross the street. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the marked pedestrian crosswalk disguised as a regular visitor, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station. The city intersection camera and municipal traffic control board detect the impossible all-green light timing and dispatch a traffic officer immediately.

briefing.plainSummary: In this scenario (T1595.002, Jeffrey Appel & Microsoft Threat Intel, ARTEX Multi-Agent LLM Framework: Machine-Speed Kill-Chain Compression, Storm-0940 Spray & Defender XDR Disruption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: aRTEX Planner-Worker LLM Initialization, then machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence, then 5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ARTEX Planner-Worker LLM Initialization, then Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence, then 5-Minute Cloud Secret Exfiltration, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. steps.plainTitle: Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence (T1505.003), Automated Kerberoasting (0x17) & Lateral Pivot
steps.storyAnalogy: Opening the unlocked cabinet panel, the impostor rewires the corner traffic light timer so every lane turns green at once and steers a yellow taxi down a side alley. Here in Step 2 inside the city street, the intruder moves quietly past the marked pedestrian crosswalk into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the neighboring sidewalk cafe.
steps.simpleExplanation: Without waiting for human operator review, the ARTEX Planner parses the valid credential output and immediately dispatches a Lateral Movement Worker agent that drops an obfuscated web shell for persistence, enumerates Active Directory SPNs (servicePrincipalName=*), requests RC4-downgraded Kerberos TGS tickets (EventID 4769, EncryptionType = 0x17), and pivots across hybrid servers in under 15 minutes (logged in Windows Security Event 4769 with KillChainCompression=Initial Spray to Web Shell + Kerberoast in 8 minutes 32 seconds, TicketEncryptionType=0x17 , RC4-HMAC Downgrade, MITRE T1558.003, WebShellParent=w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe / powershell.exe , T1505.003 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Worker-Persist: curl -X PUT https://10.10.20.14/owa/auth/healthcheck.aspx (Web shell drop via compromised admin session) (which executes the HTTP/HTTPS transfer client , Worker-Persist: curl -X PUT https://10.10.20.14/owa/auth/healthcheck.aspx , Web shell drop via compromise so that delivers the network exploit payload or retrieves the next-stage execution script , T1505.003 during "Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence , T1505.003, Automated Kerberoasting , 0x17 & Lateral Pivot" over HTTP/HTTPS). Next, the follow-up artifact Worker-AD: Invoke-Kerberoast / Rubeus.exe kerberoast /rc4opsec (Requests EventID 4769 TGS with TicketEncryptionType = 0x17) runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1505.003 during "Machine-Speed Web Shell Persistence , T1505.003, Automated Kerberoasting , 0x17 & Lateral Pivot" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 across the topology from ARTEX Go Planner-Worker LLM Agent Console , Next.js + DeepSeek/OpenAI API and Perimeter VPN / Entra ID Identity Edge , Storm-0940 Password Spray toward Hybrid Windows Server , Web Shell Staging & RC4 Kerberoasting and Microsoft Defender XDR , Automatic Attack Disruption & KQL Burst Sensor.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Windows Security Event 4769 (recording KillChainCompression=Initial Spray to Web Shell + Kerberoast in 8 minutes 32 seconds, TicketEncryptionType=0x17 , RC4-HMAC Downgrade, MITRE T1558.003, WebShellParent=w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe / powershell.exe , T1505.003 under T1505.003): Enable Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules in Block mode (Block web shell creation for Servers, Block credential stealing from LSASS), enforce AES-only Kerberos encryption (0x12), and monitor Defender for Identity for rapid SPN enumeration.
